```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

Rachedi F, Jreich R, Sparks S, Zaher A, An Haack K, Granados A, Meng Z.
*Clinical modeling of motor function to predict treatment efficacy and enable
in silico treatment comparisons in infantile-onset Pompe disease.* CPT
Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol. 2025;14(11):1797.
[doi:10.1002/psp4.13287](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13287)

Pompe disease is a lysosomal glycogen-storage disorder treated by enzyme
replacement therapy (ERT) with alglucosidase alfa (ALGLU) or its successor
avalglucosidase alfa (AVAL). Rachedi 2025 links the change in motor function to
the change in urinary hexose tetrasaccharide (uHex4), a biomarker of glycogen
burden, with two nonlinear random-coefficient (NLRC) models: one for the Gross
Motor Function Measure-88 (GMFM-88) total percent score and one for the Quick
Motor Function Test (QMFT) total raw score. Each was fitted jointly to
infantile-onset (IOPD, Mini-COMET, n = 21) and late-onset (LOPD, COMET,
n = 100) patients. Both are packaged here, one file per endpoint, as the
authors fitted them.

| Model | Output | Driver |
|---|---|---|
| `Rachedi_2025_avalglucosidaseAlfa_gmfm88` | `gmfm88cfb`, GMFM-88 total percent score change from baseline | relative change in uHex4 |
| `Rachedi_2025_avalglucosidaseAlfa_qmft` | `qmftcfb`, QMFT total raw score change from baseline | relative change in uHex4 |

The models have no ODE and no dose. Treatment acts only through the
time-varying covariate `URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL` (the relative
change from baseline in uHex4, -0.5 = a 50% fall), which the user supplies from
observed data or from a model of the biomarker. For patient *i* at visit *j*:

$$
\Delta \text{score}_{ij} = \text{shift}_i +
  \text{max}_i \left(1 - e^{-\text{rate}_i \cdot (-\text{URINARY\_HEXOSE\_TETRASACCHARIDE\_REL}_{ij})}\right)
  + \varepsilon_{ij}, \qquad \log \text{rate}_i \sim N(\text{mean}_r, \sigma_r^2)
$$

where `shift` collects the population-specific intercept and the
median-centred baseline-covariate effects, and `max` is the population-specific
asymptote of motor improvement.

```{r load-models}
mod_gmfm <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rachedi_2025_avalglucosidaseAlfa_gmfm88"))
mod_qmft <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rachedi_2025_avalglucosidaseAlfa_qmft"))
```

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- mod_gmfm$population
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Field = names(pop), Value = vapply(pop, as.character, character(1))),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

Baseline characteristics by arm are in Supplementary Table S2 and the pooled
distributions, with the medians used for centring, in Supplementary Figure S2.
The IOPD patients had all been treated with ALGLU before entering Mini-COMET
(prior treatment 4.2-7.4 years on average by arm); the LOPD patients in COMET
were treatment-naive. GMFM-88 was scored on all five dimensions in Mini-COMET
and on the standing and walking/running/jumping dimensions only in COMET.

# Source trace

| Element | Value (GMFM-88 / QMFT) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Model structure (IOPD) | `shift + max * (1 - exp(-rate * (-%dUHex4 * 0.01)))` | Main text equations, GMFM-88 and QMFT results sections |
| Model structure (LOPD) | same form, LOPD covariates | Supplementary Results equations (see Errata for QMFT) |
| `lrate` (mean_r, shared) | -0.97 / -1.19 | Tables 2 and 3 (and S3, S4), footnote a "Same for IOPD and LOPD" |
| `etalrate` = exp(log sigma_r)^2 | exp(0.34)^2 = 1.974 / exp(0.52)^2 = 2.829 | Tables 2 and 3 row "Log error of the log rate" |
| `addSd` = exp(log sigma_e) | exp(1.20) = 3.320 / exp(1.02) = 2.773 | Tables 2 and 3 row "Log residual error" |
| `int_iopd` | 2.24 / 1.51 | Tables 2 and 3 row "Intercept" |
| baseline score effect, IOPD | -0.02 / -0.03 per point | Tables 2 and 3 |
| log baseline uHex4 effect, IOPD | -2.30 / -3.34 | Tables 2 and 3 |
| log age at diagnosis effect, IOPD | 1.55 / 1.66 | Tables 2 and 3 |
| prior ALGLU duration effect, IOPD | -0.39 / -0.45 per year | Tables 2 and 3 |
| female sex effect, IOPD | 2.56 / 2.81 | Tables 2 and 3 |
| `lmax_iopd` (Max0, log) | 0.90 / 1.69 | Tables 2 and 3 |
| prior ALGLU duration on log max, IOPD | -0.55 per year / (none) | Table 2 "Max [Duration of previous ALGLU experience in years]" |
| `int_lopd` | -0.78 / 0.06 | Tables S3 and S4 |
| baseline score effect, LOPD | -0.00 / -0.10 per point | Tables S3 and S4 |
| log baseline uHex4 effect, LOPD | 0.69 / 0.35 | Tables S3 and S4 |
| log age at diagnosis effect, LOPD | -3.37 / (none) | Table S3 |
| log age at first infusion effect, LOPD | (none) / -3.78 | Table S4 |
| log baseline creatine kinase effect, LOPD | -0.97 / -0.79 | Tables S3 and S4 |
| log baseline creatinine effect, LOPD | -4.23 / (none) | Table S3 |
| log baseline BMI effect, LOPD | (none) / -2.18 | Table S4 |
| `lmax_lopd` (Max0, log) | 2.40 / 2.35 | Tables S3 and S4 |
| Centring medians, IOPD | uHex4 53.81 mmol/mol; GMFM-88 67.74; QMFT 24; age at diagnosis 0.26 y | Figure S2 dashed lines |
| Centring medians, LOPD | uHex4 8.03; GMFM-88 84.67; QMFT 41; age at diagnosis 46.63 y; age at first infusion 47.84 y; CK 550 IU/L; creatinine 52 umol/L; BMI 26.3 | Figure S2 dashed lines |
| Centring value, prior ALGLU duration | 7 years | Not printed; see Assumptions |

# Closed-form check

The models are algebraic, so the solved output must equal the published
equations evaluated by hand. With the random rate set to its median the check
is deterministic, and the two sides differ only by floating-point error.

```{r closed-form}
typ_gmfm <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_gmfm, "omega")
typ_qmft <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_qmft, "omega")

# One observation row per grid point on a single subject; `time` is only an
# index because the models have no time dimension.
motor_eval <- function(model, output, covs) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_len(nrow(covs)), amt = 0, evid = 0L)
  ev <- cbind(ev, covs)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(covs))
  s[[output]]
}

hand_gmfm <- function(d) {
  rate <- exp(-0.97)
  with(d, ifelse(
    DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE == 1,
    2.24 - 0.02 * (SCORE_GMFM88 - 67.74) -
      2.30 * (log(URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE) - log(53.81)) +
      1.55 * (log(AGE_DIAGNOSIS) - log(0.26)) -
      0.39 * (T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA - 7) + 2.56 * SEXF +
      exp(0.90 - 0.55 * (T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA - 7)) *
        (1 - exp(-rate * (-URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL))),
    -0.78 - 0.00 * (SCORE_GMFM88 - 84.67) +
      0.69 * (log(URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE) - log(8.03)) -
      3.37 * (log(AGE_DIAGNOSIS) - log(46.63)) -
      0.97 * (log(CPK) - log(550)) - 4.23 * (log(CREAT) - log(52)) +
      exp(2.40) * (1 - exp(-rate * (-URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL)))
  ))
}

hand_qmft <- function(d) {
  rate <- exp(-1.19)
  with(d, ifelse(
    DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE == 1,
    1.51 - 0.03 * (SCORE_QMFT - 24) -
      3.34 * (log(URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE) - log(53.81)) +
      1.66 * (log(AGE_DIAGNOSIS) - log(0.26)) -
      0.45 * (T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA - 7) + 2.81 * SEXF +
      exp(1.69) * (1 - exp(-rate * (-URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL))),
    0.06 - 0.10 * (SCORE_QMFT - 41) +
      0.35 * (log(URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE) - log(8.03)) -
      3.78 * (log(AGE) - log(47.84)) - 2.18 * (log(BMI) - log(26.3)) -
      0.79 * (log(CPK) - log(550)) +
      exp(2.35) * (1 - exp(-rate * (-URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL)))
  ))
}

# A grid that moves every covariate away from its centring value, in both
# populations, so each term of the equations is exercised.
set.seed(1)
n_grid <- 40
cov_grid <- data.frame(
  DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE = rep(c(1L, 0L), each = n_grid / 2),
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL = runif(n_grid, -0.9, 0.2),
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE = c(runif(n_grid / 2, 15, 150), runif(n_grid / 2, 2, 30)),
  SCORE_GMFM88 = runif(n_grid, 10, 100),
  SCORE_QMFT = runif(n_grid, 2, 64),
  AGE_DIAGNOSIS = c(runif(n_grid / 2, 0.02, 1), runif(n_grid / 2, 18, 75)),
  AGE = c(runif(n_grid / 2, 1, 12), runif(n_grid / 2, 18, 78)),
  T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA = c(runif(n_grid / 2, 0.5, 14), rep(0, n_grid / 2)),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_grid, 1, 0.5),
  CPK = runif(n_grid, 100, 3000),
  CREAT = runif(n_grid, 15, 100),
  BMI = runif(n_grid, 14, 40)
)

err_gmfm <- motor_eval(typ_gmfm, "gmfm88cfb", cov_grid) - hand_gmfm(cov_grid)
err_qmft <- motor_eval(typ_qmft, "qmftcfb", cov_grid) - hand_qmft(cov_grid)
c(gmfm88 = max(abs(err_gmfm)), qmft = max(abs(err_qmft)))
# Same parameters on both sides, so only floating-point error separates them.
stopifnot(max(abs(err_gmfm)) < 1e-8, max(abs(err_qmft)) < 1e-8)
```

A worked value: a typical IOPD patient at every centring value with a 50% fall
in uHex4 has a GMFM-88 change of
2.24 + exp(0.90) * (1 - exp(-exp(-0.97) * 0.5)) = 2.66 points.

```{r worked-value}
at_median_iopd <- data.frame(
  DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE = 1L, URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL = -0.5,
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE = 53.81, SCORE_GMFM88 = 67.74,
  SCORE_QMFT = 24, AGE_DIAGNOSIS = 0.26, AGE = 6.85,
  T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA = 7, SEXF = 0L, CPK = 1442, CREAT = 17.68, BMI = 17.05
)
worked <- motor_eval(typ_gmfm, "gmfm88cfb", at_median_iopd)
worked
stopifnot(abs(worked - 2.6647) < 1e-3)
```

# Motor response to the uHex4 decrease

The asymptotes differ sharply between the populations: exp(0.90) = 2.5 GMFM-88
points in IOPD against exp(2.40) = 11.0 in LOPD, and exp(1.69) = 5.4 against
exp(2.35) = 10.5 QMFT points. The random rate is very wide (log-scale SD 1.40
for GMFM-88, 1.68 for QMFT), so the population-mean response (averaged over
200 simulated rates) rises faster than the response at the median rate.

```{r response-curves}
uhex_grid <- seq(0, -0.8, by = -0.02)
n_rate <- 200

curve_df <- function(model, typ_model, output, endpoint, iopd) {
  covs <- data.frame(
    DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE = iopd,
    URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL = uhex_grid,
    URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE = if (iopd == 1) 53.81 else 8.03,
    SCORE_GMFM88 = if (iopd == 1) 67.74 else 84.67,
    SCORE_QMFT = if (iopd == 1) 24 else 41,
    AGE_DIAGNOSIS = if (iopd == 1) 0.26 else 46.63,
    AGE = 47.84, T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA = if (iopd == 1) 7 else 0,
    SEXF = 0L, CPK = 550, CREAT = 52, BMI = 26.3
  )
  typical <- motor_eval(typ_model, output, covs)
  ev <- merge(data.frame(id = seq_len(n_rate)), cbind(time = seq_along(uhex_grid), covs))
  ev <- ev[order(ev$id, ev$time), ]
  ev$amt <- 0
  ev$evid <- 0L
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  pop_mean <- as.numeric(tapply(s[[output]], s$time, mean))
  rbind(
    data.frame(endpoint = endpoint, population = if (iopd == 1) "IOPD" else "LOPD",
               uhex4_pct = 100 * uhex_grid, change = typical, curve = "median rate"),
    data.frame(endpoint = endpoint, population = if (iopd == 1) "IOPD" else "LOPD",
               uhex4_pct = 100 * uhex_grid, change = pop_mean, curve = "population mean")
  )
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
curves <- bind_rows(
  curve_df(mod_gmfm, typ_gmfm, "gmfm88cfb", "GMFM-88 (percent score)", 1L),
  curve_df(mod_gmfm, typ_gmfm, "gmfm88cfb", "GMFM-88 (percent score)", 0L),
  curve_df(mod_qmft, typ_qmft, "qmftcfb", "QMFT (raw score)", 1L),
  curve_df(mod_qmft, typ_qmft, "qmftcfb", "QMFT (raw score)", 0L)
)

ggplot(curves, aes(uhex4_pct, change, colour = population, linetype = curve)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  labs(
    x = "uHex4 change from baseline (%)",
    y = "Motor score change from baseline",
    colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Motor improvement as uHex4 falls, at the centring covariate values"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The duration of prior ALGLU treatment lowers both the intercept and, for
GMFM-88, the asymptote (Table 2): each extra year multiplies the IOPD
improvement ceiling by exp(-0.55) = 0.58, the effect the Discussion attributes
to patients who had been declining on ALGLU before entering Mini-COMET.

```{r prior-duration}
prior_grid <- expand.grid(prior = c(2.8, 7, 9), uhex = uhex_grid)
prior_covs <- data.frame(
  DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE = 1L,
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL = prior_grid$uhex,
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE = 53.81, SCORE_GMFM88 = 67.74,
  SCORE_QMFT = 24, AGE_DIAGNOSIS = 0.26, AGE = 6.85,
  T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA = prior_grid$prior,
  SEXF = 0L, CPK = 1442, CREAT = 17.68, BMI = 17.05
)
prior_grid$change <- motor_eval(typ_gmfm, "gmfm88cfb", prior_covs)

ggplot(prior_grid, aes(100 * uhex, change, colour = factor(prior))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  labs(
    x = "uHex4 change from baseline (%)",
    y = "GMFM-88 change from baseline (points)",
    colour = "Prior ALGLU (years)",
    title = "IOPD typical patient: effect of prior ALGLU treatment duration"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Comparison against observed arm means (Figure S1)

Supplementary Figure S1 plots, for every trial arm and visit, the observed mean
motor change against the observed mean uHex4 change. The maintainers digitised
both panels (circles: Mini-COMET, IOPD; triangles: COMET, LOPD). The uHex4 axis
values read from the two panels agree to within 0.3 percentage points, which
checks the digitisation. The models have no time dependence, so each point is
predicted from its uHex4 change alone. Visit labels are not needed and are not
carried for the COMET points.

```{r figure-s1-data}
fig_s1 <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(endpoint = "gmfm88cfb", population = "IOPD", arm = "ALGLU then AVAL 40",
             uhex4_pct = c(-8.6, -18.3, -56.6, -22.2, -50.3), observed = c(3.44, 6.20, 8.31, 9.41, 9.85)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "gmfm88cfb", population = "IOPD", arm = "AVAL 20 then 40",
             uhex4_pct = c(-10.9, 0.4, -22.9, -20.0, -35.0), observed = c(1.19, 2.62, 4.61, 3.98, 5.04)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "gmfm88cfb", population = "IOPD", arm = "AVAL 40",
             uhex4_pct = c(-11.9, -38.6, -26.1, -56.6, -54.0), observed = c(2.61, 3.82, 5.36, 8.17, 2.86)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "gmfm88cfb", population = "LOPD", arm = "ALGLU 20 then AVAL 20",
             uhex4_pct = c(-54.1, -46.2, -46.2, -25.7, -24.3, -19.4, -10.7),
             observed = c(1.23, 2.40, 0.87, 1.55, 1.65, 1.12, 2.30)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "gmfm88cfb", population = "LOPD", arm = "AVAL 20",
             uhex4_pct = c(-62.1, -60.6, -58.0, -55.5, -53.8, -53.5, -35.9),
             observed = c(3.77, 4.66, 4.02, 4.16, 4.70, 3.42, 2.38)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "qmftcfb", population = "IOPD", arm = "ALGLU then AVAL 40",
             uhex4_pct = c(-8.7, -18.3, -56.7, -22.2, -50.5), observed = c(3.34, 3.60, 6.80, 6.99, 7.16)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "qmftcfb", population = "IOPD", arm = "AVAL 20 then 40",
             uhex4_pct = c(-10.9, 0.3, -23.0, -20.0, -35.1), observed = c(-1.49, -0.16, 0.01, -1.66, 0.51)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "qmftcfb", population = "IOPD", arm = "AVAL 40",
             uhex4_pct = c(-12.1, -38.8, -26.2, -56.8, -54.1), observed = c(2.00, 3.67, 4.63, 5.29, 3.30)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "qmftcfb", population = "LOPD", arm = "ALGLU 20 then AVAL 20",
             uhex4_pct = c(-54.3, -46.4, -46.3, -25.5, -24.2, -19.5, -10.8),
             observed = c(2.14, 2.26, 1.86, 1.46, 1.86, 0.94, 1.77)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "qmftcfb", population = "LOPD", arm = "AVAL 20",
             uhex4_pct = c(-62.4, -60.8, -58.2, -55.6, -53.9, -53.5, -36.0),
             observed = c(3.94, 4.68, 4.18, 4.00, 4.29, 3.47, 2.14))
)
```

Each arm is simulated as 200 virtual patients carrying the arm's mean baseline
characteristics from Table S2. Sex is assigned in the arm's female proportion,
and the random rate is drawn per patient. Creatine kinase, creatinine and BMI
are not reported by arm, so the LOPD arms take the Figure S2 medians, which
zeroes those terms.

```{r arm-covariates}
arm_covs <- data.frame(
  population = c("IOPD", "IOPD", "IOPD", "LOPD", "LOPD"),
  arm = c("ALGLU then AVAL 40", "AVAL 20 then 40", "AVAL 40", "ALGLU 20 then AVAL 20", "AVAL 20"),
  frac_female = c(4 / 6, 1 / 6, 5 / 9, 24 / 49, 24 / 51),
  AGE_DIAGNOSIS = c(5.1 / 12, 1.9 / 12, 2.3 / 12, 48.2, 44.7), # Table S2; IOPD in months
  AGE = c(4.7, 7.7, 7.4, 50.4, 46.0),
  T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA = c(4.2, 7.4, 7.1, 0, 0),
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE = c(52.2, 80.2, 50.0, 8.7, 12.7),
  SCORE_GMFM88 = c(50.4, 54.8, 72.4, 79.1, 80.8),
  SCORE_QMFT = c(20.7, 23.3, 31.0, 42.3, 41.3)
)
knitr::kable(arm_covs, digits = 3)
```

```{r figure-s1-simulate}
n_per_arm <- 200

simulate_arm <- function(model, output, a, obs) {
  ev <- expand.grid(time = seq_len(nrow(obs)), id = seq_len(n_per_arm))
  ev <- ev[order(ev$id, ev$time), ]
  ev$amt <- 0
  ev$evid <- 0L
  ev$URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL <- obs$uhex4_pct[ev$time] / 100
  ev$DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE <- as.integer(a$population == "IOPD")
  ev$SEXF <- as.integer(ev$id <= round(n_per_arm * a$frac_female))
  for (nm in c("AGE_DIAGNOSIS", "AGE", "T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA",
               "URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE", "SCORE_GMFM88", "SCORE_QMFT")) {
    ev[[nm]] <- a[[nm]]
  }
  ev$CPK <- 550
  ev$CREAT <- 52
  ev$BMI <- 26.3
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(ev))
  obs$predicted <- as.numeric(tapply(s[[output]], s$time, mean))
  obs
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)
cmp <- list()
for (ep in c("gmfm88cfb", "qmftcfb")) {
  model <- if (ep == "gmfm88cfb") mod_gmfm else mod_qmft
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(arm_covs))) {
    a <- arm_covs[k, ]
    obs <- fig_s1[fig_s1$endpoint == ep & fig_s1$population == a$population & fig_s1$arm == a$arm, ]
    cmp[[length(cmp) + 1]] <- simulate_arm(model, ep, a, obs)
  }
}
cmp <- bind_rows(cmp) |>
  mutate(
    endpoint = ifelse(endpoint == "gmfm88cfb", "GMFM-88", "QMFT"),
    difference = predicted - observed
  )

ggplot(cmp, aes(uhex4_pct)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = observed, colour = arm, shape = "observed (Figure S1)"), size = 2.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = predicted, colour = arm, shape = "predicted"), size = 2.2) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = uhex4_pct, y = observed, yend = predicted, colour = arm), alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(endpoint ~ population, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("observed (Figure S1)" = 16, "predicted" = 4)) +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  labs(
    x = "Mean uHex4 change from baseline (%)",
    y = "Mean motor score change from baseline",
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
    title = "Arm-level observed vs predicted means (replicates Figure S1)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

```{r figure-s1-summary}
cmp_summary <- cmp |>
  group_by(endpoint, population) |>
  summarise(
    n_points = n(),
    median_difference = median(difference),
    median_abs_difference = median(abs(difference)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cmp_summary |>
  rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint, "Population" = population, "Points" = n_points,
    "Median (pred - obs)" = median_difference,
    "Median |pred - obs|" = median_abs_difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# The arm means of six to nine IOPD patients are noisy, and arm-mean covariates
# pushed through log terms are not the mean of the per-patient terms, so the
# check is on the centre of the differences. A wrong sign, a dropped "1 -" or a
# mis-scaled asymptote moves these medians by several points.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cmp_summary$median_difference) < 1.5),
  all(cmp_summary$median_abs_difference < 2.5)
)
```

The predictions follow the observed arm means in both populations. The
largest misses are in the small IOPD arms. The AVAL 20 then 40 arm is
under-predicted on GMFM-88 by about 3 points: its mean baseline uHex4 (80.2)
is the highest of the three arms and carries a log effect of -2.30, and the
arm's six patients improved more than that typical-value term implies.

# Errata check: the printed LOPD QMFT equation

The Supplementary Results print the LOPD QMFT model with
`max * exp(-rate * (-%dUHex4 * 0.01))`, without the leading `1 -` that the
Methods base model and every other printed equation carry. Read literally, a
typical LOPD patient with no uHex4 change would show a QMFT gain of about
exp(2.35) = 10.5 points. Figure S1 places every arm at 0 at baseline, and the
COMET arms never exceed 5 points. The model therefore uses the `1 -` form.

```{r lopd-errata}
lopd_median <- data.frame(
  DIS_INFANTILE_ONSET_POMPE = 0L, URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_REL = 0,
  URINARY_HEXOSE_TETRASACCHARIDE_BASE = 8.03, SCORE_GMFM88 = 84.67,
  SCORE_QMFT = 41, AGE_DIAGNOSIS = 46.63, AGE = 47.84,
  T_PRIOR_ALGLUCOSIDASE_ALFA = 0, SEXF = 0L, CPK = 550, CREAT = 52, BMI = 26.3
)
c(
  packaged_form = motor_eval(typ_qmft, "qmftcfb", lopd_median),
  printed_form = 0.06 + exp(2.35) * exp(-exp(-1.19) * 0)
)
```

# Not reproduced: Figure 4 (in silico trials)

Figure 4 drives these models with uHex4 profiles simulated by the Pompe
quantitative systems pharmacology model of Kaddi et al. (Clin Pharmacol Ther
2024, doi:10.1002/cpt.3498) for six ALGLU / AVAL regimens. That model is not in
nlmixr2lib, so the regimen comparison cannot be regenerated here. Given a uHex4
profile from any source, the comparison is a direct application of the models
above.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Prior ALGLU duration centring value.** The equations centre the duration at
  the pooled IOPD median, but Figure S2 shows it only per Mini-COMET arm
  (2.8, 7.9 and 8.3 years). The maintainers centred it at a rounded 7 years. A
  different centring value shifts the IOPD intercept by -0.39 (GMFM-88) or
  -0.45 (QMFT) points per year of difference and rescales the IOPD GMFM-88
  asymptote by exp(-0.55) per year.
- **Centring values are read from Figure S2.** The dashed lines annotated on
  Figure S2 are taken as the medians named in the equations. They are not the
  means: for the IOPD uHex4 line (53.81 mmol/mol) the n-weighted mean of the
  Table S2 arm means would be 59.3.
- **LOPD QMFT `Max0` is on the log scale.** Table S4 does not tag `Max0` with
  "(log)" as the other three tables do. The Methods state that the motor
  asymptotes were log-constrained, and exp(2.35) = 10.5 is in line with the
  LOPD GMFM-88 asymptote exp(2.40) = 11.0.
- **Log-scale baseline covariates.** The printed equations write every
  baseline-covariate term as a plain deviation from the median, but Tables 2,
  3, S3 and S4 label the uHex4, age, creatine kinase, creatinine and BMI rows
  "(log)", and the Methods say log transformation was used for some continuous
  baseline characteristics. Read on the linear scale the coefficients are
  implausible: the LOPD creatine kinase term alone would subtract
  0.97 * (1500 - 550) = 921 GMFM-88 points from a patient at 1500 IU/L. The
  table labels are therefore followed, as differences of logs. The baseline
  motor score and the prior ALGLU duration, which the tables do not mark
  "(log)", stay linear.
- **Variance parameters.** The tables report the log of the standard
  deviations. The between-patient variance of the log rate is
  `exp(log sigma_r)^2` and the additive residual SD is `exp(log sigma_e)`. The
  residual error is shared by both populations.
- **The paper's simulation summary.** For its in silico trials the paper
  generated 1000 random rates per patient and summarised them by the mean
  before computing the motor response. That is a simulation choice, not part
  of the fitted model. The packaged models draw one rate per patient, as the
  NLRC model specifies.
- **Figure S1 arm-level check.** Arm-mean covariates from Table S2 stand in for
  the individual baseline data. LOPD creatine kinase, creatinine and BMI, which
  are not reported by arm, are set to their Figure S2 medians.
- **Sensitivity model not packaged.** A lag variant linking the motor change to
  the average uHex4 change over the current and previous visit (Figure S5) was
  examined and not retained by the authors. Only the final models are packaged.

# Errata

- The Supplementary Results equation for the LOPD QMFT model omits the `1 -` of
  the exponential-asymptote term (see the check above). The equation also
  labels the age-at-infusion coefficient `beta_age at infusion,IOPD` although
  it is an LOPD parameter (Table S4).
- Table S2 labels the prior ALGLU duration row "n (%)" although it reports
  means and SDs in years.
